citeAs: Awadalla, A., Xue, L., Lo, O., Shu, M., Lee, H., Guha, E., Jordan, M., Shen, S., Awadalla, M., Savarese, S., Xiong, C., Xu, R., Choi, Y., Schmidt, L. (2024). MINT-1T: Scaling Open-Source Multimodal Data by 10x: A Multimodal Dataset with One Trillion Tokens. arXiv:2406.11271.
creator: Anas Awadalla, Le Xue, Oscar Lo, Manli Shu, Hannah Lee, Etash Guha, Matt Jordan, Sheng Shen, Mohamed Awadalla, Silvio Savarese, Caiming Xiong, Ran Xu, Yejin Choi, Ludwig Schmidt (University of Washington, Salesforce Research, Stanford University, University of Texas at Austin, University of California Berkeley)
description: MINT-1T-PDF-CC-2024-18 is the PDF subset of MINT-1T sourced from CommonCrawl WAT files (February 2023 to April 2024 dumps), containing multimodal interleaved documents with sequences of images and text extracted from PDF files. It is part of MINT-1T, the largest open-source multimodal interleaved dataset with one trillion text tokens and 3.4 billion images total, including 93 billion tokens from the PDF subset.
name: MINT-1T-PDF-CC-2024-18
rai:dataBiases: The PDF subset has a higher proportion of Science and Technology documents compared to HTML or OBELICS, likely due to the nature of scientific communication where PDFs are the preferred format for sharing research papers and technical reports. The authors note they avoid using text quality classifier models as they have been shown to favor text from certain demographics. The dataset may contain content considered confidential, offensive, or sensitive (race, ethnic origins, sexual orientations, religious beliefs, political opinions, financial or health data) as it is sourced from the public web.
rai:dataCollection: PDF documents are sourced from CommonCrawl WAT files from February 2023 to April 2024 dumps. PDF links are extracted from these dumps, then downloaded and read using PyMuPDF. PDFs larger than 50MB or over 50 pages are discarded. Pages with no text are excluded. Reading order is obtained by finding bounding boxes of text blocks, clustering by columns, and ordering top-left to bottom-right. Images are anchored based on proximity between image bounding boxes and text blocks on the same page.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: PDF documents sourced from CommonCrawl WAT files. For PDFs, the text and image reference numbers are released along with the URL for the PDF. Raw data is not provided as it may contain offensive content.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Data collected from January 2024 to June 2024. PDF source documents come from CommonCrawl WAT dumps from February 2023 to April 2024.
rai:dataLimitations: PDF parsing has two noted limitations: (1) PyMuPDF sometimes fails to detect images; (2) PDFs have arbitrary layouts, so in some cases an incorrect reading order is extracted (e.g., incorrectly reading across column boundaries or starting from the rightmost column). The dataset is not self-contained and relies on downloading external image URLs, with no guarantees these URLs will remain available over time (link rot). The dataset may contain confidential, offensive, or sensitive content despite filtering efforts. The dataset should not be used to train models that ingest or generate personally identifying information or for military applications.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Reading order extraction: bounding boxes of text blocks on each PDF page are found, blocks are clustered based on columns, and ordered from top-left to bottom-right. Images are anchored in the sequence based on proximity between the image's bounding box and text blocks on the same page. During model training (not dataset construction), 50% of HTML, 45% of PDF, and 5% of ArXiv documents are sampled for the interleaved mixture.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: PDF documents undergo: (1) size filtering — PDFs over 50MB or 50 pages are discarded; (2) text quality filtering using RefinedWeb methods (removing excessive duplicate n-grams, MassiveText rules); (3) non-English document removal using Fasttext language identification (confidence threshold 0.65); (4) NSFW URL substring filtering; (5) image filtering — images smaller than 150px or larger than 20,000px removed; aspect ratio threshold of 3 applied (to preserve scientific figures); (6) NSFW image detection using a deep neural network classifier; (7) PII removal — email addresses replaced with templates, IP addresses replaced with randomly generated non-functional IPs; (8) paragraph and document deduplication using Bloom Filter (false positive rate 0.01, 13-gram paragraphs); (9) image deduplication using SHA256 hashes (images appearing more than 10 times within a snapshot removed).
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset will be distributed as JSON shards through the HuggingFace interface. The authors will actively respond to issues and maintain the dataset. Updates will be communicated through the README in the HuggingFace interface. Older versions can be found using the Git history of the dataset repository. An erratum will be present on the README of the HuggingFace dataset page. A Google form will be provided for opting data out of MINT-1T. Contributions can be made through the Pull Request mechanism of the HuggingFace interface.
rai:dataSocialImpact: MINT-1T is intended to make research into large multimodal models more accessible by providing a large-scale open-source dataset. The authors took steps to remove personally identifiable information (masking emails and IP addresses) and NSFW content. However, the dataset may still contain harmful content from the web. Using the dataset to train models that ingest or generate personally identifying information or for military applications is considered inappropriate. A Google form will be provided for individuals to request removal of their data from MINT-1T.
rai:dataUseCases: Pre-training large multimodal models that can process multiple interleaved images and text. Other potential uses include training models for generating interleaved image-text sequences and building multimodal document retrieval systems. Inappropriate uses include training models to ingest or generate personally identifying information and military applications.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Fasttext language identification model (confidence threshold 0.65) for non-English document removal; NSFW image detector (GantMan/nsfw_model deep neural network) for pornographic/undesirable image removal; GPT-4 used to classify LDA topic words into domains for diversity analysis; GPT-2 tokenizer used for token count analysis; PyMuPDF for PDF parsing and reading order extraction.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset may contain images of individuals and text about specific individuals sourced from the public web. It may also contain sensitive data such as race or ethnic origins, sexual orientations, religious beliefs, political opinions, financial or health data, and biometric data. Email addresses and IP addresses are masked (replaced with templates). The dataset may also contain content that is considered confidential. Subpopulations are not explicitly identified but such information may be extractable from the dataset.

null_reasons.rai:annotationsPerItem: No human annotation was performed; data is automatically collected and filtered from CommonCrawl PDFs.
null_reasons.rai:annotatorDemographics: No crowdworkers or human annotators were involved; only the authors of the work were involved in data collection.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: No human annotation was performed; no inter-annotator agreement metrics applicable.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: No annotation platform used; data collection was automated from CommonCrawl PDFs.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: No human annotation protocol; data is automatically extracted and filtered.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The paper states 'None' for missing information from individual instances; no explicit discussion of missing data handling beyond standard filtering.
null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: No imputation protocol described; missing or invalid data is discarded rather than imputed.
